title: Point and Distance
story: You're building a map app! Two friends are at different locations — you need to calculate the distance between them so they can meet up.
why: Point structs are a classic use case — they model coordinates, and distance methods teach you to work with multiple struct instances in one method.
analogy: A Point is like a pin on a map. The distance method is like stretching a measuring tape between two pins to see how far apart they are.
try_it: Create a third Point for a friend's house. Find the distance from home to friend, and from school to friend. Which one is closer?
tips: Use `math.sqrt()` for square roots — you pass one Float64 number and get a Float64 back
The `dx` and `dy` variables keep the formula readable — compute them first, then combine
Methods can take other instances of the same type: `fn Point.distance_to(self, other: Point)`
common_mistakes: Subtracting in the wrong order: `other.x - x` instead of `x - other.x` — squaring makes either work, but be consistent
Using `^` for exponent — in XIOM, `dx * dx` is the correct way to square, not `dx ^ 2`
Forgetting to use `math.sqrt` — just `sqrt(...)` won't work without the `math.` prefix
